lines: SMS Organizer was downloaded over a million times, and it sorted every message on the phone itself.
People loved what it did. Reviews kept asking for an app that looked the part.
Two navigation bars competed for attention, text was small and low in contrast, reminders stopped at the alert, and some messages arrived in languages readers couldn't read.
First, I moved the main navigation to the bottom, within thumb reach, and turned the top bar into message filters.
Larger text and stronger contrast cleared the rest of the noise, and the update asks people before it moves anything.
Reminders used to stop at the alert.
Now the app creates them from booking messages, groups them by type, and a tap opens the next step, like hotels at your destination.
An SMS arrives in whatever language the sender chose.
So people pick their language once, then translate any message into it or hear it read aloud, and every layout holds when a translation runs long.
In UX Labs testing, people preferred the new design for its layout and modern look.
It shipped on a Material three design system I built. Engagement rose thirty percent.
Redesigning an app people already use is a migration as much as a launch.
